target_customer: Parents of children aged 4 to 10 who pay a monthly subscription; later homeschooling families
problem: Kids learn science from YouTube and passive video; parents want interactive, standards aligned science lessons delivered by engaging presenters.
business_model: Consumer subscription, about 9 dollars per month average, free to schools

founders.name: Chad Swenson
founders.background_notes: Built an interactive evolution learning project as a senior project eight years before December 2020 (TechCrunch).

founders.name: Tanner Swenson
founders.background_notes: Chad's brother. Named by TechCrunch (Dec 2020); not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Lawrence Tran
founders.background_notes: Met Chad while consulting at Bill.com. YC page lists the line Hawaii to California.

competitors.name: YouTube
competitors.what: Free video platform kids already use for science learning, contrasted with Tappity by TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: A video and quiz app on iOS; the hard part was producing a large library of high quality live action lessons, not the engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Content library and presenters took effort to produce but rivals like Mystery Science and Outschool could add interactive video; no network effect.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Tappity; it later added homeschool courses.

market_need_then: In December 2020 TechCrunch reported over 5,000 paying customers, more than 20,000 weekly active users and about 30 million lessons completed, and the company was profitable when it applied to YC; remote learning during Covid raised parent demand.

identity.mascot_or_character: Live action human presenters such as Haley, the science expert, instead of a cartoon mascot

branding.brand_signature: Live action presenters teaching interactive lessons

brand_strength.rationale: A playful name that fits the tap interaction, but no press or community evidence about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Tappity was a small, already profitable subscription app of interactive science lessons that raised a $1.3M seed in December 2020 with Mystery Science and Toca Boca founders among backers. It is listed as active with a small team and has extended into homeschool courses, but no later round, exit or growth data was found, so the outcome is a quiet small business rather than a proven venture scale result.
notes: YC page and a Product Hunt style listing call it W20 in some aggregators; the directory says Summer 2020. An aggregator reports $1.45M total, unverified. Headquarters reported variously as Palo Alto, San Francisco and Burbank. The company website snippet now advertises open and go science courses for homeschoolers; the date of that shift is unknown. No source on the name origin.
